Last week, responsibilities for crate labels
New handlers should know what to do first

This page explains the Companion Animal Travel Desk process for preparing animal travel files at Aurelia Skyways, because careful handling protects the animal, supports the traveler, and prevents avoidable delays. New staff must begin by reviewing the booking, confirming the species, and checking whether the animal needs special care, since humane handling depends on accurate information before any crate or cabin decision is made. <<FACT F076>> When the record is complete, compare the animal's condition with the carrier rules and make sure the traveler understands what will happen next.

In routine cases, keep your language calm and direct. If a traveler appears uncertain, explain the process in plain terms and avoid rushing the conversation. The handler should note any signs of stress, protect the animal from unnecessary noise, and select the least disruptive option that remains within policy. For a rabbit, the travel review must be especially careful, and you must pass along the inserted guidance exactly as recorded in the system file. Do not add comments around it, and do not guess or paraphrase. The same method applies when a bird is part of the booking. <<FACT F059>> After that, confirm the rest of the preparation without introducing extra details that might confuse the traveler.

Crate checks must be exact. Measure the carrier only against the approved standard, inspect the doors, and verify that the interior allows the animal to stand, turn, and rest comfortably. A small dog requires particular attention because a carrier that is too large can shift in transit, while one that is too narrow creates strain. <<FACT F068>> If the crate fails inspection, arrange correction before acceptance, and keep the tone professional throughout the discussion.

Always record what you observed, what you advised, and what the traveler agreed to do. Care plans should reflect the animal's temperament, the route, and the likely stress points of the journey. Remember that clear notes, calm speech, and careful checks are the standards to remember.
